title: Network ops onboarding snapshot and audit probe (WIP)
content:
PURPOSE:
This is a working sketch of an operator-friendly onboarding runbook and audit sampling plan for customer-managed networking (VPCs / private interconnect) in Redwood Private. Primary goals: surface the minimal set of audit events for compliance, define approval checkpoints during customer handover, and provide a lightweight sampling strategy to reduce signal noise while preserving forensics.

SCOPE:
- Applies to Private deployments where customers provide VPC and manage NAT/firewalls (customer-managed networking).
- Covers core handover steps from infra provisioning -> onboarding -> first 30 days of traffic.
- Focused on audit logs, approval gates, retention and pragmatic sampling. Not a full security design.

AUDIENCE:
- Solutions engineering (customer onboarding)
- Platform ops and SREs supporting Private installs
- Security/compliance reviewers and customer security contacts
- Product PMs owning Private networking capabilities

HIGH-LEVEL HANDOVER FLOW (draft):
1) PRE-HANDOFF (solutions engineer): collect networking manifest, expected CIDR ranges, KMS info, service endpoints, contact roster. checklist below.
2) NETWORK CONNECTIVITY VALIDATION (SRE + Customer): run connectivity tests, BGP/peering verification, egress rules, MTU checks. Record results as artifacts.
3) APPROVAL GATE #1 (Network Readiness): internal SE signs off that manifest matches customer topology. (Who: SE; What: manifest OK).
4) DEPLOY & INSTRUMENT (Platform): create customer stack, enable audit pipeline, configure KMS key access, apply minimal logging.
5) APPROVAL GATE #2 (Audit & KMS): Security or Compliance approves log collection config + KMS policy. (Who: Security reviewer).
6) HANDOVER (Customer contact + SE): run acceptance tests and make stepwise traffic cutover.
7) PROBING WINDOW (0-30 days): increased sampling, daily health checks, weekly audit sampling review.
8) APPROVAL GATE #3 (Stable): After 30d, customer and SE agree to production SLA and normal sampling rate.

CHECKLIST (quick):
- [ ] Manifest received: VPC ids, CIDR, subnets, AZ mapping, route tables
- [ ] KMS key ARN + IAM principals documented
- [ ] Firewall / ACL baseline (egress/ingress) documented
- [ ] Admin contact + incident rotation schedule
- [ ] Expected peak qps and p99 latency targets
- [ ] Any regulatory constraints (PCI / HIPAA / GDPR notes)

AUDIT EVENTS TO CAPTURE (recommended minimal set):
- CONTROL PLANE ACTIONS:
  - admin_authz: who granted/revoked platform roles (fields: actor, target_role, action, timestamp, request_id)
  - kms_key_access: decrypt/encrypt or grant events to customer KMS keys (fields: principal, operation, key_id, timestamp, request_id)
  - network_config_change: route table, firewall, peering changes (fields: actor, object, before, after, timestamp, ticket_id)
- DATA PLANE & ACCESS:
  - control_plane_api_call: create/start/stop model endpoints, deployments (fields: actor, endpoint_id, action, model_version, timestamp)
  - admin_console_login: console sessions that escalate privileges (fields: user, ip, mfa, timestamp, session_id)
- AUTOMATION & DEPLOYMENT:
  - infra_pipeline_run: automated deploy runs, success/failure, diff summary (fields: pipeline_id, status, changed_files, timestamp)
- ALERTS FOR INVESTIGATION (derived):
  - anomalous_kms_usage: bursty decrypts from unusual IPs or principals
  - config_drift_alert: detected divergence from manifest (requires periodic comparison)

NOTE: for each event type above we should standardize the following minimal schema fields: timestamp, request_id, actor, action, object_id, outcome, region, correlated_ticket_id. Keep lightweight to avoid enormous index costs.

AUDIT LOG RETENTION & SAMPLING STRATEGY (proposal):
- Raw verbatim event retention: 90 days hot, then 1 year cold (encrypted).
- Index/derived summaries: 365 days.
- Sampling window: first 30 days after handover = 100% capture for all types. After that, keep 100% for control_plane_action and kms_key_access; sample data-plane logs at 10% with rate-limited bursts when anomalies are detected.
- Rationale: 30-day window gives forensics for initial troubleshooting; keep critical items always-on.

AUDIT STORAGE & ENCRYPTION NOTES:
- Logs written to customer-designated S3/GCS bucket when customer mandates. Otherwise write to Redwood encrypted bucket with customer-specific prefix.
- All persisted artifacts encrypted with customer KMS when provided; otherwise use Redwood-managed Envelope keys.
- Access to logs requires role-based gating + approval ticket (see approval matrix).

APPROVAL MATRIX (sketch):
- SE (solutions engineer): approves manifest correctness and customer acceptance.
- Platform lead / Oncall SRE: approves connectivity tests and deploy readiness.
- Security reviewer: approves audit config & KMS policies.
- Customer security: signs off on access model and any egress rules that impact their compliance.

EXAMPLE LOG LINES (human-readable examples we can use in doc samples):
- 2025-02-21T15:12:03Z | request_id=PD-57231 | actor=se+mchen@redwood | action=network_config_change | object=rt-0a12b3 | before=10.0.0.0/24 | after=10.0.0.0/22 | ticket=JIRA-PD-1123
- 2025-02-22T03:40:11Z | request_id=PD-57255 | actor=infra-bot | action=infra_pipeline_run | status=FAIL | pipeline=deploy/customer-acme | changed_files=network/route.tf
- 2025-02-23T08:09:59Z | request_id=PD-57333 | actor=cust-admin@acme | action=kms_key_access | operation=Decrypt | key_id=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:alias/acme-key

ESCALATION & ROLLBACK TRIGGERS (initial thought):
- If anomalous_kms_usage or admin_authz for unexpected principals -> immediate pause of sensitive operations and paged to security oncall.
- If network_config_change that causes >5% error rate increase within 15m of change -> auto rollback and SE/Platform paging.
- Rollback must be scripted in infra pipeline with an auditable request id.

PROBING PLAN (operational checks during first 30d):
- Daily ingest check: confirm audit pipeline delivered 100% of control plane events. Simple script: count_by_type yesterday vs expected.
- Weekly sampling review: a 1-hour triage with SE + Security to surface any weird patterns.
- Monthly metric: mean time to detect (MTTD) for config drift during the probing window.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- [ ] Decide exact retention tiers for regulated customers (PCI/HIPAA) — legal to weigh in. (Priya)
- [ ] Implement a minimal schema validator (JSON schema) for event payloads (Diego)
- [ ] Define RBAC flow for customer access to logs vs Redwood access (who requests, approval ticket pattern) (SRE + Security)
- [ ] Determine default sampling percentages for medium vs high churn deployments
- [ ] Draft a short customer-facing one-pager explaining what logs Redwood collects and how they can request exports

NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep this doc compact; large tables belong in the Confluence PRD. Use Drive for smaller checklists and the on-call runbook snippets.
- When we move to in_review, attach sample Kibana queries and dashboard screenshots (placeholder).

REFERENCES:
- Confluence: PD Private Deployments onboarding checklist (link above)
- JIRA PD-1123 (network handover epic)
- Internal PR: github.com/redwood/repo/private-deployments/pull/448

END OF WIP DOCUMENT.
